messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

message.content:
**Typical difference:**  
- **Los Angeles (Pacific Time)** is usually **UTC‑8** in winter and **UTC‑7** in summer.  
- **Berlin (Central European Time)** is usually **UTC +1** in winter and **UTC +2** in summer.  

Because both regions shift their clocks at roughly the same time of year, the time difference is normally **9 hours** (Berlin is ahead).

**When it can be 8 hours**

The U.S. and Europe change their clocks on slightly different dates:

| Period | U.S. DST | Europe DST | Time difference |
|--------|----------|------------|-----------------|
| Early March (after U.S. DST starts, before Europe does) | UTC‑7 | UTC +1 | **8 hours** |
| Late March–Late October (both in DST) | UTC‑7 | UTC +2 | **9 hours** |
| Late October–Early November (Europe DST ended, U.S. still in DST) | UTC‑7 | UTC +1 | **8 hours** |
| Rest of the year (both in standard time) | UTC‑8 | UTC +1 | **9 hours** |

So, for most of the year Berlin is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles, but during the short windows when only one side is observing daylight‑saving time, the gap shrinks to 8 hours.

So after US DST ends but before Europe DST ends? Actually Europe DST ends earlier (Oct). So after Oct, Europe standard UTC+1; US DST still UTC-7 until Nov 5. So difference 8 hours.
